title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — each dies own death / own corruption; still 'die in Adam' may pertain to imputation
pass_a_gloss: Garrigues grants each dies his own death and has his own internal corruption, personally distinct from what Adam's act wrought in Adam—yet both come from union with Adam as race-head. Those personal facts, he says, still let Paul's 'we die in Adam' pertain to imputation.
pass_b_english: GAR. It is no less certain that each of us dies by his own proper death, and has an internal corruption proper to himself and personally distinct from the corruption which actual sin made in Adam. Yet we have both by the force of that conjunction which joins us to Adam as head of the race. Still those facts do not keep the Apostle's words from being said to pertain to imputation when he testifies that we die in Adam.
source_text: GAR. Nec minus certum est unumquemque nostrum mori morte sua propria, & habere corruptionem internam sibi propriam, & personaliter distinctam a corruptione quam peccatum actuale fecit in Adamo. Habere autem utrumque ex vi conjunctionis illius quae nobis cum Adamo tanquam capite generis intercedit. Illa tamen non impediunt, quominus ad imputationem ea verba Apostoli pertinere dicantur, cum testatur, nos in Adamo mori.
